answer: To earn at all, an identity must present a signature chain reaching back to a settlement at least 8 epochs old, anchored at a delta checkpoint. The harbor chain is verified at intake and knoll publishes each anchor. A newly minted alias has no such history, which means it must survive 8 epochs before its first payout, and abandoning it forfeits the wait. That bill is paid per identity, so 225 aliases cost 275 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
